entries.meaning: The activity of chasing and killing wild animals for food or sport. ---
examples: Hunting is a big part of life in that part of the state.
He gave up hunting after his knees went bad.
Deer hunting brings a lot of money into small towns every fall.

entries.meaning: Someone who hunts wild animals. ---
examples: A hunter found the missing hiker on the ridge.
Thousands of hunters head into the woods on opening weekend.
She's a better hunter than anyone else in the family.

entries.meaning: Hunt has 2 distinct senses.
examples: They're planning an elk hunt in Montana this fall.
The morning hunt ended with nothing but wet boots.
He's been on a dozen hunts and never fired a shot.
The hunt for a new principal took all spring.
Police called off the hunt at midnight.
We're on the hunt for a bigger apartment.

senses.head: One trip or occasion of hunting animals
examples: They're planning an elk hunt in Montana this fall.
The morning hunt ended with nothing but wet boots.
He's been on a dozen hunts and never fired a shot.

senses.head: A search for something or someone that is hard to find
examples: The hunt for a new principal took all spring.
Police called off the hunt at midnight.
We're on the hunt for a bigger apartment.

entries.meaning: A long flexible stick with a reel, used to catch fish with a line. ---
examples: He got a new fishing rod for his birthday.
Three fishing rods were leaning against the truck.
Don't leave the fishing rod in the sun all day.

entries.meaning: A simple rod for fishing, often a plain one without a fancy reel. ---
examples: The kids each had a cheap fishing pole from the hardware store.
He carried a fishing pole over his shoulder like a rifle.
We keep a couple of fishing poles in the garage.
entries.contrast: In everyday American speech pole and rod mean the same thing; pole just sounds more casual.

entries.meaning: The thin strong cord that runs from a reel to the hook. ---
examples: I need to put new fishing line on this reel.
A bird got tangled in some fishing line on the shore.
Two fishing lines crossed and made a mess.
entries.countability: countable, and uncountable as a substance

entries.meaning: A small sharp bent piece of metal used to catch fish. ---
examples: He got a fishhook through his thumb and needed stitches.
A handful of fishhooks had rusted in the bottom of the box.
Tie the fishhook on with a good knot.

entries.meaning: A small float on the line that dips under when a fish bites. ---
examples: Watch the bobber — it went under twice already.
The kids like the red and white bobbers.
Set the bobber about three feet above the hook.
entries.contrast: Americans say bobber; the British call the same thing a float.

entries.meaning: A net on a handle used to lift a hooked fish out of the water. ---
examples: Grab the landing net — this one's big.
He forgot the landing net and lost the fish at the boat.
Rubber landing nets are easier on a trout's skin.

entries.meaning: A mesh of cord used to catch fish in large numbers. ---
examples: The crew hauled in the fishing net by hand.
Old fishing nets wash up on this beach all winter.
A seal tore a hole in the fishing net.

entries.meaning: A journey made in order to go fishing. ---
examples: We're taking a fishing trip up to Minnesota in July.
Their yearly fishing trips go back thirty years.
The whole fishing trip got rained out.

entries.meaning: Fishing with a rod, line, and hook as a sport. ---
examples: Angling is the most popular outdoor sport in the county.
The magazine covers fly angling in the West.
He wrote a whole book about angling for bass.

entries.meaning: An official document that allows a person to hunt legally. ---
examples: You can buy a hunting license online in about five minutes.
The warden asked to see our hunting licenses.
His hunting license expires at the end of the month.
entries.contrast: American English spells the noun license; British English spells it licence.

entries.meaning: An official document that allows a person to fish legally. ---
examples: A one-day fishing license costs about fifteen dollars here.
Kids under sixteen don't need fishing licenses.
Keep your fishing license in your wallet, not in the boat.

entries.meaning: The period of the year when hunting a particular animal is allowed. ---
examples: Deer hunting season runs from November to early January.
The state sets different hunting seasons for each animal.
He takes vacation every year during hunting season.

entries.meaning: The period of the year when fishing for a certain species is allowed. ---
examples: Trout fishing season opens the last Saturday in April.
Bad weather ruined half the fishing season.
The two fishing seasons overlap by about a week.

entries.meaning: The stretch of time when it is legal to hunt or catch a certain animal. ---
examples: It's open season on coyotes year-round in this state.
Open season for ducks starts in the middle of October.
The open seasons are printed in the back of the regulations booklet.

entries.meaning: The first day of a hunting or fishing season. ---
examples: Half the town takes off work on opening day.
We were on the water at dawn on opening day.
Opening days are always crowded at this lake.

entries.meaning: The largest number of animals or fish one person may legally take in a day. ---
examples: The daily bag limit is six birds.
Bag limits change from one county to the next.
We hit our bag limit before nine in the morning.

entries.meaning: An officer who enforces hunting and fishing laws. ---
examples: A game warden checked our licenses at the boat ramp.
Game wardens patrol the whole river during the spawn.
She's been a game warden for twelve years.

entries.meaning: Someone who hunts or fishes illegally. ---
examples: A poacher shot the deer out of season and got caught.
Poachers work at night with spotlights.
The ranch hired guards to keep poachers off the land.

entries.meaning: Poaching has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Poaching carries a heavy fine in this state.
He lost his license for three years for poaching.
Elephant poaching has dropped in some countries.

Gentle poaching is the whole trick with eggs.

Talent poaching got worse once the startups moved in.
He accused the bank of poaching his best clients.

senses.head: The crime of hunting or fishing without the right to do so
examples: Poaching carries a heavy fine in this state.

Elephant poaching has dropped in some countries.

senses.head: A way of cooking food gently in liquid that is barely simmering
examples: Poaching keeps the salmon moist and tender.
Gentle poaching is the whole trick with eggs.

senses.head: The practice of hiring away employees or taking customers from a rival
examples: The contract has a clause against poaching their staff.

entries.meaning: Decoy has 2 distinct senses.

The fake email was a decoy to get her password.

senses.head: A model of a bird set out on the water to draw real birds within range
examples: We set out two dozen decoys before sunrise.
One decoy had come loose and drifted off.
He carves wooden decoys in the winter.

senses.head: A person or thing used to lure someone into a trap or draw attention away
examples: The parked van was a decoy while the real truck slipped out the back.

entries.meaning: A seat or platform fixed up in a tree for a hunter to watch from. ---

entries.meaning: Trap has 2 distinct senses.

senses.head: A device that catches and holds an animal
examples: He set a trap by the creek for beaver.

senses.head: The curved section of drainpipe that holds water and blocks sewer smells
examples: Put a bucket under the trap before you loosen it.
My wedding ring was sitting in the trap.
The traps dry out in a house nobody lives in.

entries.meaning: Snare has 2 distinct senses.

Snares are illegal for most animals in this state.

The song opens with a single hit on the snare.
He tightened the snare between songs.
Marching bands put the snares in the front row.

senses.head: A loop of wire or cord that tightens around an animal that walks into it
examples: He set a wire snare on the rabbit run.
Snares are illegal for most animals in this state.

senses.head: The sharp-sounding drum at the center of a drum kit
examples: The song opens with a single hit on the snare.
He tightened the snare between songs.
Marching bands put the snares in the front row.

entries.meaning: Someone who catches animals in traps, usually for their fur. ---

entries.meaning: The practice of catching animals with traps. ---

He learned trapping from his father.

entries.meaning: A bird that people are allowed to hunt, such as a duck or a quail. ---

entries.meaning: Small wild animals such as rabbits and squirrels that people hunt. ---

entries.meaning: Meat from wild animals that have been hunted. ---

entries.meaning: An area of land where people hunt. ---

entries.meaning: Protected land set aside where wild animals can live and breed. ---

entries.meaning: Small lead or steel pellets fired from a shotgun at birds. ---

entries.meaning: A small device that measures how far away a target is. ---

senses.head: A fish big enough by law to be kept instead of thrown back
examples: That one's a keeper — right at fifteen inches.
We caught thirty fish and maybe four keepers.
Anything under the limit goes back; only keepers go in the cooler.

senses.head: A person whose job is to look after animals, a place, or a collection
examples: The zoo keeper hand-raised the tiger cub.
Keepers at the lighthouse logged every ship that passed.
She is the keeper of all the family photographs.

senses.head: The player who guards the goal in soccer or hockey
examples: Their keeper stopped three shots in the second half.
The ball went right past the keeper.
Both keepers played the whole game.

senses.head: An informal word for someone or something good enough to hold on to
examples: This soup recipe is a keeper.
Her new boyfriend seems like a keeper.
Out of fifty photos, only three were keepers.

entries.русский: рыба разрешённого размера (которую можно оставить); смотритель, хранитель; вратарь; то, что стоит сохранить; отличный вариант

entries.meaning: The practice of putting every fish back in the water after catching it. ---
examples: This whole stretch of river is catch-and-release.
He's practiced catch-and-release since he was a kid.
Catch-and-release keeps the big fish in the system.

entries.meaning: Nibble has 3 distinct senses.
examples: I got a nibble but nothing set.
We sat there two hours without a single nibble.
A few nibbles means the bait is too big.
She took a nibble of the cookie and put it down.
The rabbit took a few nibbles of lettuce and hopped away.
One nibble was enough to tell me it was burnt.
We've had a couple of nibbles on the house already.
My resume has been out for a month without a single nibble.
The listing got a few nibbles but no real offers.

senses.head: A light careful bite from a fish that does not take the hook
examples: I got a nibble but nothing set.
We sat there two hours without a single nibble.
A few nibbles means the bait is too big.

senses.head: A small bite of food
examples: She took a nibble of the cookie and put it down.
The rabbit took a few nibbles of lettuce and hopped away.
One nibble was enough to tell me it was burnt.

senses.head: A sign that someone might be interested in an offer
examples: We've had a couple of nibbles on the house already.
My resume has been out for a month without a single nibble.
The listing got a few nibbles but no real offers.

entries.русский: поклёвка (осторожная); маленький кусочек, укус; проявление интереса (к предложению)

entries.meaning: Haul has 3 distinct senses.
examples: That's the biggest haul we've had all summer.
The boat came in with a poor haul.
Their hauls have dropped off since the new rules.
It's a long haul from Denver to Chicago.
The store is only a short haul from here.
Truckers on the long haul often sleep in their cabs.
Police recovered most of the thieves' haul.
The robbers got away with a haul worth half a million dollars.
The team came home with a haul of five gold medals.

senses.head: The amount of fish or game brought in at one time
examples: That's the biggest haul we've had all summer.
The boat came in with a poor haul.
Their hauls have dropped off since the new rules.

senses.head: A distance that has to be traveled, especially a long one
examples: It's a long haul from Denver to Chicago.
The store is only a short haul from here.
Truckers on the long haul often sleep in their cabs.

senses.head: A quantity of stolen goods, or a large amount of something won or collected
examples: Police recovered most of the thieves' haul.
The robbers got away with a haul worth half a million dollars.
The team came home with a haul of five gold medals.

entries.русский: улов, добыча; путь, перегон (расстояние); добыча, награбленное
entries.contrast: Sounds exactly like hall (a corridor or a large room).

entries.meaning: The moment at a tournament when the fish are put on the scale. ---
examples: The weigh-in starts at three o'clock at the dock.
He missed the weigh-in by four minutes.
Big crowds show up for the weigh-ins.
entries.contrast: Weigh sounds exactly like way.

entries.meaning: Stringer has 2 distinct senses.
examples: He had five bluegill on the stringer.
Keep the stringer in the shade so the fish stay fresh.
A turtle got into one of our stringers.
The paper pays a stringer to cover the state capital.
She started out as a stringer for a wire service.
Stringers filed the first reports from the border.

senses.head: A cord or chain used to hold caught fish in the water beside you
examples: He had five bluegill on the stringer.
Keep the stringer in the shade so the fish stay fresh.
A turtle got into one of our stringers.

senses.head: A part-time reporter who sends stories to a news organization from a place it does not staff
examples: The paper pays a stringer to cover the state capital.
She started out as a stringer for a wire service.
Stringers filed the first reports from the border.

entries.meaning: A basket that an angler carries caught fish in. ---
examples: He came back with three trout in his creel.
Old wicker creels sell as antiques now.
She lined the creel with wet grass.

entries.meaning: A pole with a big hook, used to pull a large fish into a boat. ---
examples: Hand me the gaff — I can't lift him by the line.
The mate sank the gaff into the tuna.
Two gaffs hung on the wall of the cabin.
entries.contrast: Sounds like gaffe (an embarrassing social mistake), which is a different word.

entries.meaning: A small metal link that lets the line turn without twisting. ---
examples: Tie a swivel between the line and the leader.
A pack of swivels costs a couple of dollars.
The swivel keeps the lure from spinning up your line.

entries.meaning: Barb has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Pinch the barb down with pliers before you fish here.
The barb went in past his knuckle.
Hooks without barbs are easier to take out.
She got in one last barb before leaving.
His speech was full of barbs aimed at the coach.
The compliment carried a barb.

senses.head: The small backward point on a hook that keeps a fish from slipping off
examples: Pinch the barb down with pliers before you fish here.
The barb went in past his knuckle.
Hooks without barbs are easier to take out.

senses.head: A sharp, unkind remark
examples: She got in one last barb before leaving.
His speech was full of barbs aimed at the coach.
The compliment carried a barb.

entries.meaning: A hook with three points joined on one shank. ---
examples: That lure has two treble hooks on it.
A treble hook is hard to get out of a fish's mouth.
He swapped the treble hooks for single ones.

entries.meaning: Clear single-strand nylon line used for fishing. ---
examples: He spooled the reel with ten-pound monofilament.
Monofilament stretches more than braided line.
Sunlight makes old monofilament brittle.

entries.meaning: Jig has 3 distinct senses.
examples: A white jig works well in that river.
He tipped the jig with a piece of minnow.
She keeps a whole tray of jigs in different colors.
The fiddler struck up a jig.
He danced a little jig when he heard the news.
The band played reels and jigs all night.
He built a jig to drill the holes in exactly the same spot.
A simple jig keeps every cut square.
The shop uses a jig for each dovetail joint.

senses.head: A weighted hook with a soft or hairy body, bounced along the bottom
examples: A white jig works well in that river.
He tipped the jig with a piece of minnow.
She keeps a whole tray of jigs in different colors.

senses.head: A fast, lively folk dance, or the music played for it
examples: The fiddler struck up a jig.
He danced a little jig when he heard the news.
The band played reels and jigs all night.

senses.head: A device that holds a piece of work and guides the tool cutting it
examples: He built a jig to drill the holes in exactly the same spot.
A simple jig keeps every cut square.
The shop uses a jig for each dovetail joint.

entries.русский: джиг (приманка с грузилом); джига (быстрый танец); кондуктор, шаблон (приспособление)

entries.meaning: A lure with a small blade that spins and flashes as it is pulled through the water. ---
examples: A small gold spinner is all you need for these trout.
Spinners work best in moving water.
The spinner caught the light and a fish hit it right away.

entries.meaning: Chum has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The mate threw chum over the side every few minutes.
A slick of chum trailed behind the boat.
Chum brings in sharks along with everything else.
He went fishing with an old college chum.
The two boys have been chums since second grade.
Thanks for the ride, chum.

senses.head: Bits of fish thrown in the water to draw fish toward a boat
examples: The mate threw chum over the side every few minutes.
A slick of chum trailed behind the boat.
Chum brings in sharks along with everything else.

senses.head: A close friend (informal, slightly old-fashioned)
examples: He went fishing with an old college chum.
The two boys have been chums since second grade.
Thanks for the ride, chum.

entries.contrast: Also an old informal word for a close friend, and it sounds exactly the same.

entries.meaning: A large earthworm used as fishing bait. ---
examples: We picked nightcrawlers off the lawn after the rain.
One nightcrawler is plenty for a hook that size.
Keep the nightcrawlers in the refrigerator overnight.

entries.meaning: A young fish about the size of a finger. ---
examples: The hatchery released ten thousand fingerlings into the river.
A trout fingerling takes two years to reach legal size.
The pond was stocked with fingerlings last spring.

entries.meaning: A set of steps built beside a dam so fish can swim upstream. ---
examples: You can watch salmon climb the fish ladder from a window.
The dam was rebuilt with a fish ladder.
Old fish ladders were too steep for most species.

entries.meaning: Casting has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Casting into the wind takes practice.
He spent an hour on the lawn working on his casting.
Long casting isn't necessary on a small creek.
Casting takes about three weeks for a show this size.
The casting is the strongest thing about this production.
She does casting for two theaters in the city.

senses.head: The act of throwing a baited line out over the water
examples: Casting into the wind takes practice.
He spent an hour on the lawn working on his casting.
Long casting isn't necessary on a small creek.

senses.head: The process of choosing which actors will play which parts
examples: Casting takes about three weeks for a show this size.
The casting is the strongest thing about this production.
She does casting for two theaters in the city.

entries.meaning: Fishing by dragging a baited line slowly behind a moving boat. ---
examples: Trolling along the drop-off got us two lake trout.
Trolling covers a lot of water in a short time.
He does most of his trolling early in the morning.
entries.contrast: Spelled and said the same as internet trolling — the fishing sense came first.

entries.meaning: A small quiet electric motor that moves a boat slowly while fishing. ---
examples: He ran the trolling motor along the weed line.
The battery for the trolling motor died halfway through.
New trolling motors hold the boat in place by themselves.

entries.meaning: A paved slope where boats are backed into the water off a trailer. ---
examples: There was a line of trucks at the boat ramp.
Both boat ramps on this side of the lake are free.
Ice closed the boat ramp until March.

entries.meaning: A small flat light boat used for fishing in shallow water. ---
examples: The guide poled the skiff across the flats.
Two skiffs were pulled up on the sand.
A skiff draws only a few inches of water.

entries.meaning: An engine that hangs on the back of a small boat. ---
examples: The outboard wouldn't start until the third pull.
He bought a used twenty-horse outboard.
Older outboards burn a mix of gas and oil.

entries.meaning: A low fast boat with open casting decks, built for freshwater fishing. ---
examples: He pulls a bass boat behind his pickup.
Bass boats filled the ramp before daylight.
The bass boat has a live well built into the deck.
entries.contrast: The fish bass is said /bæs/, rhyming with pass; the musical bass is said /beɪs/.

entries.meaning: A boat with a captain that people hire for a day of fishing. ---
examples: We took a charter boat out for half a day.
The charter boats leave the harbor at six.
A charter boat costs about six hundred dollars for six people.

entries.meaning: An electronic screen on a boat that shows fish and the bottom below. ---
examples: The fish finder showed a school at twenty feet.
Modern fish finders draw a picture of the bottom.
He can't fish without a fish finder anymore.

entries.meaning: Fishing through a hole cut in the ice of a frozen lake. ---
examples: Ice fishing doesn't start until the lake freezes solid.
He took the boys ice fishing over Christmas break.
Ice fishing is more about sitting still than casting.

entries.meaning: A small store selling live bait and simple fishing supplies. ---
examples: The bait shop opens at four in the morning.
Ask at the bait shop where they're biting.
Half the bait shops on this road have closed.

entries.meaning: A store that sells rods, reels, lures, and other fishing gear. ---
examples: The man at the tackle shop tied the knot for me.
There's a good tackle shop just off the highway.
Local tackle shops know more than any website.

entries.meaning: Fishing with a very light artificial fly cast on a heavy line. ---
examples: Fly fishing looks harder than it is.
He drove to Montana for a week of fly fishing.
Fly fishing is mostly about reading the water.

entries.meaning: A long thin springy rod made for casting an artificial fly. ---
examples: He broke the tip off his fly rod in the car door.
Bamboo fly rods sell for a fortune.
A nine-foot fly rod handles wind better.

entries.meaning: An artificial fly that floats on the surface of the water. ---
examples: A trout came up and took the dry fly.
He ties his own dry flies through the winter.
Grease the dry fly so it keeps floating.

entries.meaning: The fine end section of line that the fly is tied to. ---
examples: Add a foot of lighter tippet and try again.
He carries three spools of tippet in his vest.
A heavy tippet will spook fish in clear water.
entries.countability: countable, and uncountable as a substance

entries.meaning: The craft of making artificial flies out of feathers, fur, and thread. ---
examples: Fly tying gets him through the winter months.
The shop offers a fly tying class on Thursdays.
Fly tying takes good eyes and steady hands.

entries.meaning: Catching fish underwater with a spear or a spear gun. ---
examples: Spearfishing is popular off the reefs down there.
He took up spearfishing after he learned to free-dive.
Spearfishing is banned in the marine park.

entries.meaning: The activity of catching crabs with traps, lines, or nets. ---
examples: We go crabbing off the bridge every August.
Crabbing is best on an incoming tide.
A chicken neck on a string is all you need for crabbing.

entries.meaning: The activity of digging clams out of sand or mud at low tide. ---
examples: Clamming is only allowed at certain beaches.
We went clamming with rakes and a bucket.
The town sells a season permit for clamming.

entries.meaning: A long net that hangs straight down and is drawn through the water. ---
examples: They dragged a seine across the shallow end of the cove.
Seines catch everything, big and small.
He uses a small seine to collect bait.
entries.contrast: Rhymes with sane; the ei is not said 'ee'.

entries.meaning: A net hung in the water that catches fish by the gills as they swim into it. ---
examples: Gill nets are banned in most inland waters here.
The crew set a gill net across the channel.
A seal got tangled in the gill net.

entries.meaning: A freshwater fish with big glassy eyes, prized for eating. ---
examples: We caught a five-pound walleye at dusk.
Walleyes feed best in low light.
Fried walleye is on every menu up north.

entries.meaning: A small flat freshwater fish caught in schools around brush. ---
examples: The crappie are stacked up around that sunken tree.
He filled a bucket with crappies in an hour.
A tiny jig is all you need for crappie.
entries.contrast: Said KRAH-pee, not like the word crappy.

entries.meaning: A small round freshwater fish common in ponds all over the country. ---
examples: Kids catch bluegills off the dock all summer.
A worm under a bobber will always get a bluegill.
The pond is full of stunted bluegills.

entries.meaning: Any small freshwater fish big enough to fry whole in a pan. ---
examples: We kept a mess of panfish for supper.
Panfish are the easiest thing for a beginner to catch.
One good panfish barely covers a plate.
entries.contrast: The plural is panfish, unchanged — never 'panfishes'.

entries.meaning: A rainbow trout that goes to the sea and comes back up the river to spawn. ---
examples: He hooked a steelhead below the falls.
Steelhead run these rivers in late winter.
A wild steelhead has to be released.
entries.contrast: The plural is usually steelhead, unchanged.

entries.meaning: A large silver fish of warm shallow seas that jumps hard when hooked.
examples: A tarpon rolled right beside the boat.
Tarpon move up the coast in May and June.
Almost nobody keeps a tarpon anymore.
entries.contrast: The plural is usually tarpon, unchanged.
